notes.2: (a) This question required candidates to identify and explain why well qualified employees are important for DADS business. Many answers discussed the benefits such as improved reputation, high quality classes and that injuries were less likely if classes were taught by well qualified teachers. The highest credit for this response was given to candidates who successfully related their explanation to the dance studio and gymnasium rather than those who gave a generic answer. The best responses gained full marks by fully applying the analysis to the business in the case study. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0450 Business Studies June 2016 (b) Many candidates scored very well by calculating the current and acid test ratios for both years. Better candidates identified in the recommendation that the business had reduced liquidity and was in fact in danger of not being able to meet short-term debts. Weaker responses only considered what was happening to the figures, e.g. inventories fell by $200 or incorrectly calculated the ratios. Only the few best responses were applied to the business in the case study and were able to gain full credit.
notes.1a: The majority of candidates made a good start by correctly identifying four stakeholder groups such as Danielle and Anthony the owners, customers taking dance lessons, employees such as gym instructors, the finance manager and other businesses such as those selling dance shoes and clothing. Many responses then went on to explain the objective of each stakeholder. Some responses included Danielle and Anthony as two stakeholder groups and could only be given credit for one stakeholder group.
notes.1b: The answers to this question were generally good. Most responses discussed the advantages and disadvantages of three factors when deciding where to locate the dance studio. Strong responses demonstrated a recognition that most of their customers live near to the existing dance studio and therefore would need to be careful about moving too far away from them. Also, there was a need for a new larger building so that the business can expand. Better responses included detailed analysis earlier in the answer and then used this to compare the three factors before deciding which factor was the most important when deciding on the new location. Weaker responses were often repetitive, restating earlier points in the recommendation and hence gained no further credit or made a weak judgment selecting only one method to justify and gained some additional credit.
notes.3a: Candidates often gave answers that recognised delegating to the new manager released time for Danielle and Anthony to make better use of their time on other areas of the business such as teaching classes. Many answers did not recognise that the finance manager was not qualified to carry out marketing functions and therefore may not make good decisions about marketing. The weaker responses did not demonstrate application or showed a lack of knowledge of what is meant by delegation, discussing instead the benefits and drawbacks of employing a new manager.
notes.3b: Many of the answers to this question were good. Most candidates could offer benefits of secondary research being cheap to collect but the other two methods being more expensive. Weaker responses were focused on competitors, existing customers and parents of children who attend classes rather than the three methods of market research being used. This approach often resulted in vague answers that did not go beyond level 1. Better responses gave a consideration of the advantages and disadvantages of each method of research and then justified which method of research was the best one, thus gaining some level 3 credit. Stronger responses justified why the alternative options were rejected, gaining further level 3 credit. Weaker responses simply repeated earlier points in the recommendation, such as by using questionnaires they would find out what customers wanted. A minority of responses discussed the use of the information rather than the methods of research, which was not the focus of the question. Application was present in many answers.
notes.4a: Many responses included lower unemployment and lower spending on health care but sometimes did not go on to apply the explanation to this context. Some responses wrote about the effects on the business of an increase in the number of dance studios, which was given no credit. Many answers were generic and so could only be given limited credit. Those candidates who applied their explanation of the external benefits to the increase in the number of dance studios gained the credit available for application.
notes.4b: This question was concerned with the effects of three changes on DADS. Many candidates identified that higher levels of employment might lead to higher incomes and consequently increased number of customers for the studio although it might be harder to find suitable employees leading to increased wage rates. While an increase in annual tax paid on buildings might result in DADS reconsidering the move to larger premises due to increased costs. Finally, as more children want to dance it might mean that DADS will need to expand or it will not be able to offer more classes and take on more customers, as many classes are full. A minority of responses incorrectly stated that a reduction in unemployment would lead to fewer customers. Better responses gave a conclusion of which change would have the greatest effect on DADS based on the earlier analysis and in the context of DADS. Weaker conclusions were usually a repetition of earlier statements and gained no further credit. Answers were often well applied by referring to the need to increase the size of the business so they do not have to turn away dancers and increasing the number of classes for adults as well as children, they also recognised that dance lessons were a luxury that may be paid for if incomes were rising from higher levels of employment leading to more customers for the dance studio and gymnasium.
